newsitem.title: CHINA: China yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: China yuan ends up at two-year high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at an intraday and two-year high of 8.2913 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Tuesday, from Monday's 8.2930, with buying active below the key 8.2920 level, traders said.
The close was the highest since May 18, 1995 when the yuan ended at 8.2892.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2918 yuan.
Dealers said buying in the yuan was active again on Monday after consolidating for the past few days.
A firm close above the key 8.2920 level indicated pro-yuan sentiment was strong on the market, they said.

The yuan opened higher at 8.2918 and fell slightly to hit an intraday low of 8.2922 early in trading before moving just above the 8.2920 level for most of the session. Trading was active with most business done at 8.2916, traders said.
"Active buying was seen whenever the yuan moved below the 8.2920 level," one dealer said. "This supported the local currency and made it close firmly above that level."
A second dealer said the central bank, the People's Bank of China, did little to intervene to depress the yuan as it has often done in the past.
"If the central bank does not act to depress the local currency, the yuan is likely to breach the 8.2900 resistance level in the short term," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to continue to rise slightly on Wednesday.
The yuan closed little changed at an intraday low of 7.1438 from 7.1501 against 100 Japanese yen and up slightly at 1.0718 from 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
